Article Title: ‘From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping’: PM Modi’s heartfelt message to CWG heroes - Watch
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi interacted with India's CWG 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday. (Pic credit: PM Modi's X post)

Mirabai recalls four years of struggle

‘One family will bring three medals’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s Glasgow success

NEW DELHI: “From every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping.”Prime Minister Narendra Modi had an emotional message for Mirabai Chanu as he interacted with India's Commonwealth Games 2026 medal winners at his residence on Sunday, reflecting on the sacrifices behind the country's successful campaign in Glasgow.Modi hosted the medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg and heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys at the Games. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings.During one of the conversations, Modi recalled the emotional scenes surrounding Mirabai's gold-medal triumph.“Tears were falling from you. I feel as if from every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping,” Modi told the Olympic silver medallist.Mirabai, who won gold in Glasgow, opened up about the difficult journey that preceded her Commonwealth Games triumph, including the disappointment of the Paris Olympics.“I was very happy, and emotional too. That day the happiness was greater and I cried because at the Paris Olympics, I lost a medal by 1 kg. In a player’s life what all we have to face. So within these 4 years, how much and what all I had faced, every time injuries were going on and all that was happening.So with great difficulty I had faced these 4 years. So when all that happened, on the podium when I stood, sir, and when our flag goes up and our national anthem plays, sir, we cannot stop, sir, tears come out on their own,” she said.Modi responded by highlighting the wider impact of the athletes' achievements.“This is very good. It is not as if this achievement of yours is considered only your achievement; your victory becomes a very big inspiration for the coming generations.”The informal interaction also saw athletes share lighter and deeply personal moments from their Glasgow campaigns.Modi reminded para shot put gold medallist Sharmila Dhankar of a promise she had made earlier.“You made a promise. Last time, yours, both daughters will become players,” Modi said with a smile.Dhankar replied: “Haanji, right now they are young in age. In the next Commonwealth, one family will bring 3 medals.”Men's 100m T47 gold medallist Dilip Gavit, meanwhile, spoke about dedicating his performance to his guru.“When I was running, when my event was on 29th (July), that day was Guru Purnima, so that day I gave a gift to my guru,” he was heard saying in the video.In another video posted by Modi, gold medallist boxer Sakshi Chaudhary introduced herself and the contingent.“Hello friends! This is Sakshi Chaudhary. Today, our honourable Prime Minister has invited us, the Commonwealth Games medalists, and we feel very proud. We are extremely happy to have met him; he is very humble. Sir, would you like to say something?” she said.Modi replied with a message that summed up his interaction with the athletes: “Jo khelega, woh khilega” (The one who plays, will blossom). “Always cheer for Bharat.”India's fourth-place finish came despite a significantly smaller contingent and a reduced sporting programme compared to Birmingham 2022. India sent 122 athletes to Glasgow, compared to 210 in Birmingham, while 30 of its 61 medals in 2022 came in sports that were not part of the Glasgow programme.Despite those limitations, India retained its fourth-place position and improved its medal conversion rate, with 38 athletes returning home with medals. Long-distance runner Gulveer Singh was the only Indian athlete to win two medals.The Glasgow Games concluded after 11 days, with Scotland handing over the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India ahead of the 2030 edition in Ahmedabad.The symbols were handed to Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi during the closing ceremony.Ahmedabad will become only the second Indian city to host the Commonwealth Games after New Delhi staged the 2010 edition.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi hosted medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg. Modi heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze.

Article Title: Jannik Sinner withdraws from Cincinnati Open with knee injury, US Open return now in focus
Article Text:
Jannik Sinner (AP Photo)

Sinner, Alcaraz absent from Cincinnati

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Alcaraz also racing against time

Jannik Sinner's US Open preparations have suffered another setback after the world No. 1 withdrew from the Cincinnati Open with a right knee injury, leaving his return to competitive tennis uncertain with the hard-court Grand Slam just weeks away.Sinner, who has not played since successfully defending his Wimbledon title last month, announced his withdrawal from the Masters 1000 event on Sunday after also pulling out of the tournament in Toronto.The 24-year-old Italian said he was not yet ready to compete despite working with his medical team and will now focus on recovering in time for the US Open, which begins on August 30.“After consulting with my doctors and my team, I have to announce that I need to withdraw from the Masters 1000 tournament in Cincinnati,” Sinner said in a statement released by tournament officials.“My right knee has been bothering me and even though we have been working hard with my medical team, I have to accept that I'm not ready to compete yet. I’m very disappointed not to be able to play in Cincinnati. I can't wait to be back next year and I'm now focusing on getting ready for the US Open,” the statement added.Sinner's withdrawal comes just days after Carlos Alcaraz pulled out of Cincinnati with a lingering right wrist injury.The back-to-back withdrawals mean the tournament will be without the world's top two men's players when the singles competition begins.The timing is particularly significant for Sinner. Cincinnati has traditionally been one of the final major hard-court tune-ups before the US Open and was the tournament where he triumphed two years ago before going on to win the New York Grand Slam.Sinner enters the US Open as one of the leading contenders after winning his fifth Grand Slam title at Wimbledon. He needs only the French Open to complete a career Grand Slam.Alcaraz, meanwhile, has been sidelined since April after suffering the wrist injury and missed the French Open and entire grass-court season, including Wimbledon.The Spaniard was expected to return in Cincinnati as he prepares to defend his US Open title. Recent social media images and videos showed the seven-time Grand Slam champion practising on court, raising hopes that he would be ready for the hard-court swing.With both Sinner and Alcaraz now missing Cincinnati, their fitness will remain a major talking point heading into the final stretch before the US Open.
Article Summary: Jannik Sinner withdraws from Cincinnati Open with a right knee injury. World No. 1 has not played since successfully defending his Wimbledon title. Sinner's withdrawal comes just days after Carlos Alcaraz pulled out of Cincinnati with a lingering right wrist injury.

Article Title: BCCI CoE is not a rehabilitation centre: VVS Laxman
Article Text:
VVS Laxman (Image credit: TNN)

BCCI's CoE (Image credit: TNN)

HUNT ON FOR PATEL’S REPLACEMENT

Image credit: TNN

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

CLOSED DOOR DOMESTIC MATCHES

BENGALURU: The BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) has come under scrutiny amid a spate of recurring injuries among Indian cricketers. This is despite programmes for contracted players being laid out by the national team’s strength and conditioning coach and physio, with the CoE ensuring that the prescribed norms are followed.CoE head VVS Laxman outlined the role of the state-of-the-art facility. “CoE is not a rehabilitation centre. It is a centre where we strive for excellence every day,” the India batting great said during a media interaction at the centre here on Sunday.Laxman, whose tenure ends later this year, also refuted claims that the team management, selectors and CoE were not on the same page.“We don’t like to use the word ‘blame’ because when you use the word, then you’re finding someone as a scapegoat. There’s brilliant coordination between the COE, the team management of both the teams (men and women), the SSM (sports science and medicine) staff and the selection committee. The selector reaches out to the CoE asking for the fitness status report and we collect it and send it to the selection committee chairperson with a copy to the head coach of both the teams and the BCCI .”On the specific case of Jasprit Bumrah and Sai Sudharsan, who have been ruled out of the upcoming two-Test series against Sri Lanka after being named in the squad, subject to clearing fitness tests, Laxman and BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia, who was present along with other office bearers including president Mithun Manhas and treasurer Raghuram Bhat, cleared the air.“(With) Bumrah and Sai Sudharsan, there was always an asterisk (in the media release through which the team was named).It means subject to fitness. Bumrah and Sai Sudharsan were going to be picked for Sri Lanka subject to fitness clearance. You assess them, move them from one stage to the next and if the progression is slow, you communicate to the selection committee chairman and the head coach, which is happening seamlessly. They understand that the players are not yet ready,” explained Laxman.Weighing in on the issue, Saikia added, “Our selection meetings are held 3-4 weeks before the team departs. So at the time of team selection, we do not know the exact status of the player. If a player recovers during the period, he will be in the team. We do not outrightly reject because of the date of selection. We do not deprive players and nobody can predict the human body; the players are not machines."Laxman also asserted that players undergoing rehabilitation are not released from the centre until fitness parameters are met.“We have set certain parameters with the SSM and S&C process. Unless those benchmarks are met, or bettered, we don’t release the players. The whole idea is that when the players go back to the teams from the first match, they should be able to perform to the best of their potential,” he added.The post of head of Sports Science and Medicine (SSM) at the CoE has remained vacant since Nitin Patel left the role in March 2025.Laxman said the BCCI is yet to find a suitable candidate for the key position. Former India team physiotherapist Andrew Leipus had initially been approached but backed out after discussions. In the meantime, senior physiotherapist Dhananjay Kaushik has been overseeing the SSM department since Patel’s departure.“After Nitin left, we did not get anyone to fill the position. We had Andrew Leipus, and everything was agreed upon. In fact, Devajit (Saikia) had 2-3 meetings with him, but Andrew backed off citing family reasons,” Laxman stated.Among the criteria that is proving to be a stumbling block is the fact that the position is based out of Bengaluru.“We conducted a full-fledged interview process and shortlisted five candidates and No 1 was an Australian. He also backed out, saying he cannot move to Bengaluru. It is a full-time job. It is day-to-day monitoring. Another professional, the head of sports science at the All Blacks (New Zealand rugby team), almost agreed, but he also backed off at the last moment.”“To fill in the position, you require not someone of the stature but the knowledge and understanding of Indian cricketers. But a lot of credit goes to the professionals who are already in the team because they have stepped up,” added Laxman.While the grounds at the CoE are picturesque and state-of-the-art, one of the facility’s biggest drawbacks is that matches are played behind closed doors. The BCCI acquired the land from the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (KIADB), and under the applicable rules, galleries cannot be erected as the facility is designated as a training centre.This has proved challenging, with spectators often seen perched on trees or standing along the expansive compound wall, particularly when international stars are in action.With the domestic season opener — the Duleep Trophy — set to be played at the Centre, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said, “There are some government restrictions and we cannot have a crowd in this campus. But this year, we have increased the number of matches to be telecast live. That way, we are giving the fans an opportunity to watch their favourite players and teams.”Saikia added that the BCCI was open to moving the Duleep Trophy final to a stadium where spectators could be allowed.“We still have time. We'll look into that aspect. If required, we'll do that,” he added.
Article Summary: The BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) has come under scrutiny amid a spate of recurring injuries among Indian cricketers. This is despite programmes for contracted players being laid out by the national team’s strength and conditioning coach and physio. CoE head VVS Laxman outlined the role of the state-of-the-art facility. He refuted claims that the team management, selectors and CoE were not on the same page.

Article Title: Spin threat looming, selectors rope in Sarfaraz Khan for Sri Lanka series
Article Text:
Sarfaraz Khan (AP Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The national selection committee has fallen back on Sarfaraz Khan as Sai Sudharsan’s replacement for the two-Test series in Sri Lanka starting on Aug 15.Sarfaraz was kept out of the scheme of things after India lost a Test series 0-3 against New Zealand at home in 2024. He did travel to Australia for the subsequent Test tour but wasn’t given any matches.Sarfaraz will join the team in Colombo on Monday after the BCCI on Sunday announced Sudharsan was still recovering from a stress reaction on his right toe.The selectors seemed to have moved on from Sarfaraz when they started ignoring him for India ‘A’ teams after the England tour in 2025.TOI understands that the selectors and the team management now felt the need to have a batter seasoned on spinning tracks.With a FirstClass average of 64 in 62 matches, the selectors thought the 28-year-old Mumbai middle-order batter was the best option. Ruturaj Gaikwad was identified as a prospective Test middle-order option by the selectors, but his poor performance for India ‘A’ in Sri Lanka last month didn’t offer much confidence to the selectors.Gaikwad averages 44 in 47 First-Class matches.The other name doing the rounds was Andhra’s Shaik Rasheed.But with India’s World Test Championship (WTC) chances hanging by a thread, the selectors and team management went by the experience of Sarfaraz given the young Indian batters’ recent struggles against spin at home.Sarfaraz had lost the confidence of the team management when he failed to get going against New Zealand on turning tracks despite scoring a 150 in the first Test of the series.Then Test captain Rohit Sharma too didn’t play him in the XI in Australia.The selectors had picked him for India ‘A’ for the tour of England last year. Sarfaraz had scored a 92 but wasn’t picked again, nor did he feature in the India ‘A’ team’s tour of Sri Lanka last month
Article Summary: Sarfaraz will join the team in Colombo on Monday. Sai Sudharsan is still recovering from a stress reaction on his right toe. Ruturaj Gaikwad was identified as a prospective Test middle-order option by the selectors.

Article Title: Ashmita Chaliha first Indian to win Korea Masters
Article Text:
Ashmita Chaliha (Image credit: BAI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Twenty-six-year-old Ashmita Chaliha authored an impressive comeback to stun fourth seed Han Qian Xi of China in the final 14-21, 21-14, 21-14, and become the first Indian ever to win the Korea Masters Super-300 in Incheon on Sunday.The left-hander from Guwahati needed just 53 minutes to turn the final on its head, capping a week in which she had already announced herself as a genuine threat after dismantling top seed Hina Akechi in the quarterfinals.With this win, the World No. 50 vaults into an elite bracket of Indian shuttlers to have tasted Super 300 success — a list headlined by Saina Nehwal and PV Sindhu , and now bolstered by a fresh wave of talent that includes Devika Sihag, who won in Thailand in Feb, and Tanvi Sharma, who lifted the Chinese Taipei Open trophy just last week.It is raining titles for India. After Sindhu’s maiden Japanese Open title triumph on July 19, Indian women have won three titles in the last four weeks. Only last Sunday, Tanvi Sharma became the youngest Taipei Open winner.For Ashmita, however, the Korea Masters title carries a significance of its own. It is her first BWF World Tour crown and a landmark moment after a long road back from injury.The final initially appeared to be slipping away from her. Chaliha made a bright start, opening up a 4-0 lead and moving 9-5 ahead.But Xi fought back strongly, levelling at 11-11 before producing a decisive run of points to seize control. The Chinese shuttler eventually closed out the opening game 21-14.Ashmita later revealed that the biggest obstacle was not her opponent, but the tricky drift at one end of the court. Rather than allowing the difficult conditions to disrupt her rhythm, the Indian adapted.A change of ends in the second game brought greater comfort, allowing her to control the shuttle better and construct rallies with more patience.At 6-6, Ashmita began asserting herself. She combined powerful smashes with sharp defensive returns to break away. She led 11-8 at the interval and continued to dictate the exchanges, moving 17-10 ahead before sealing the game 21-14 with another attacking winner.The decider became a test of nerve and tactical intelligence. Ashmita moved into an early 5-2 lead, but Xi responded and went into the mid-game interval 11-9 ahead.The Indian, however, refused to let the momentum disappear. Ashmita looked a different player after the break as she scored seven straight points to move to 16-11.The Indian made no mistake, completing a remarkable turnaround and sealing her maiden World Tour title.“I feel really great and unbelievable. But then I am trying to digest it. Now, I am hungry for more,” Ashmita said after the match.Her assessment of the contest underlined how much the victory was built on adaptation.“In the first game, it was a little bit tricky because of the drift condition, so I was not able to manage it. But in the second, the other side was more comfortable and there was less drift, so I was able to control it. And in the third, after 11 points, I changed again — so I was on the good side. So I’m glad that I could pull off.”The triumph is particularly significant given the setbacks Ashmita has overcome. She suffered a tear in her right knee during the Korea Open in 2024, forcing her to undergo surgery and an extensive rehabilitation programme.She returned to competition in February the following year and went on to play 14 events. This year, after competing in a couple of tournaments, she spent three months building the strength required to handle the demands of a full BWF calendar.The hard work began to show with back-to-back quarterfinal appearances at the China Masters and Malaysia Masters, followed by a semifinal finish at the Macau Open.Training under Park TaeSang at the National Centre of Excellence in Guwahati, Ashmita arrived in Korea ranked World No. 50. She leaves as a Super 300 champion.“All credit goes to coach Park. Without him I could not have been this much energetic,” Ashmita said.
Article Summary: Ashmita Chaliha is the first Indian to win the Korea Masters Super-300 title. The left-hander from Guwahati beat Han Qian Xi of China in the final. It is her first BWF World Tour crown and a landmark moment after a long road back from injury.

Article Title: As coach, I have to take care of their feelings and emotions also: Tan Kim
Article Text:
Satwiksairaj Rankireddy (Image credit: X)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: After a month-long absence from the badminton court due to a shoulder injury, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy is making a return to the game at the World Championships beginning in New Delhi early next week.Satwik has been out of action with a recurring shoulder injury and has not played a competitive tournament for almost a month. Though there are concerns regarding his match sharpness and physical condition, his coach Tan Kim He allayed those fears and is optimistic of his ward’s fitness.“He is getting better and I can say he is ready to play,” Tan said.Having won a bronze at the Tokyo World Championship four years ago and also last year in Paris, the Satwik-Chirag Shetty combo will be keen to win the elusive championship on their home turf.But Tan feels there is little point in putting unnecessary pressure on the pair.“We can’t win every tournament. The important part is to maintain consistency and, of course, try to win a major tournament. For this World Championships, we will take it one match at a time,” he said.Tan added that the presence of sparring partners has helped replicate the intensity of competition, but the biggest emphasis now is on the players’ mindset.The Malaysian coach, who has worked with Satwik and Chirag since the early stages of their rise, has also seen the pair evolve. Their attacking game has long been regarded as their biggest weapon. But Tan believes their defensive game has improved significantly.“They used to be more focused on attacking, but now they are much, much better defensively,” he said.With the draw out, the pair’s preparation will be rival-specific.“We normally watch the game of the opponents and they will watch our game as well. We need to be careful if the opponents change their game during the match,” Tan said.Tan’s own approach has also changed as Satwik and Chirag have grown from promising youngsters into established world-class players. Earlier, the coach could simply give instructions and expect them to follow. Today, he believes discussions are equally important.“They are no longer juniors. Earlier, whatever I told them, they would just follow. Now they are world class players, so we have a lot of discussion,” he said.For Tan, coaching the pair is no longer only about badminton. Understanding their emotions, fatigue and mental state has become equally important.“I’m not just watching them for badminton. Sometimes I have to take care of their feelings and emotions also. Before they start, I sit down with them and ask a lot of questions to make sure they are ready,” he said.
Article Summary: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy is making a return to badminton after a month out with a shoulder injury. His coach Tan Kim He is optimistic of his ward's fitness and says he is ready to play. The Satwik-Chirag Shetty combo will be keen to win the elusive championship.

Article Title: Hezly Rivera becomes first US woman after Simone Biles to win back-to-back gymnastics titles since 2012
Article Text:
Hezly Rivera

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Hezly Rivera has shown that she is no longer the young newcomer who surprised everyone at the Paris Olympics. The 18-year-old Olympic gold medallist won her second straight US women's gymnastics title after overcoming a fall on the uneven bars earlier in the competition. Rivera finished with a two-day total of 111.950 points, more than one point ahead of runner-up Claire Pease.Her victory made her the first American woman other than Simone Biles to win back-to-back national titles since former world and Olympic champion Jordyn Wieber achieved the feat in 2011 and 2012.From Olympic underdog to national championRivera described herself as an “underdog” two years ago when she was selected for the US Olympic team for Paris. She was the youngest and least-known member of a highly experienced team that won the women's team gold medal. It was the Americans' third team Olympic title in four Games.While several of her Olympic teammates, including Biles and Suni Lee, have taken extended breaks from competition, Rivera has continued to compete.Lee announced last month that she had started training again with the aim of returning to competition.Rivera won her first national title in New Orleans last year after edging Leanne Wong.Rivera's hopes of defending her title looked uncertain after she fell face-first onto the mat during the uneven bars competition on Thursday. She missed a release and could not stay on the apparatus. But Rivera responded strongly on the final day. She started Sunday on bars and produced a determined routine. She managed to recover from a small stall near the end before completing her dismount with a small step.Charleigh Bullock, who turned 16 last month, finished third. Reese Esponda, who trains at the Houston-area gym owned by Biles' family, took fourth place.Two-time Olympic gold medallist Jade Carey finished fifth.Carey is continuing to add difficulty to her routines as she targets a third appearance at the Olympic Games. The result also marked a homecoming for the Phoenix native.
Article Summary: Hezly Rivera won her second straight US women's gymnastics title. The 18-year- old overcame a fall on the uneven bars earlier in the competition. Rivera finished with a two-day total of 111.950 points, more than one point ahead of runner-up Claire Pease.

Article Title: Former Brazil international arrested after wife makes serious domestic violence allegation
Article Text:
Jadson has been arrested in Brazil following domestic violence allegations involving his wife, while the former Brazil international denies physical assault/Image: X

Jadson arrested after alleged domestic incident

Jadson denies physically assaulting his wife

Court grants provisional release

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Career with Brazil and Corinthians

Former Brazil international Jadson has been arrested in southern Brazil following allegations of domestic violence involving his wife. The 42-year-old, who enjoyed a successful career with clubs including Corinthians, Shakhtar Donetsk and Athletico Paranaense, has denied physically assaulting his partner, while Brazilian authorities continue to investigate the case after granting him provisional release under a series of court-imposed conditions.According to Globo Esporte , Jadson was arrested in the city of Cambé, in the southern Brazilian state of Paraná, following an alleged domestic violence incident that occurred during an argument with his wife.The outlet reported that the woman told police Jadson grabbed her by the neck with both hands and attempted to strangle her. Officers who responded to the incident reportedly observed visible marks on her neck that were consistent with her account.She also alleged that it was not the first time such an incident had occurred and requested protective measures as well as a medical injury assessment.Following his arrest, Jadson was initially taken to a police station before being transferred to Cambé State Prison.According to Globo Esporte, the former midfielder was formally investigated on suspicion of domestic violence, bodily harm and verbal abuse.During questioning by the Civil Police, Jadson acknowledged that an argument had taken place but denied using physical violence.According to Brazilian outlet Meu Timão, he described the incident as a marital dispute and insisted no physical assault had occurred.Both Jadson and the complainant were taken to the Central de Flagrantes police station without handcuffs before providing their statements to investigators.His legal team also issued a statement following the incident.According to Brazilian outlet Meu Timão , Jadson's defence said the investigation remains at an early stage and stressed that he is entitled to the presumption of innocence. The lawyers added that the court found no legal grounds to keep him in custody and said they would not discuss the case publicly while the investigation remains ongoing.According to Meu Timão, Judge Karin Feuerharmel Giuseppin, of the Londrina court, ordered Jadson's release on Sunday morning, granting him provisional freedom without requiring bail.The court imposed several precautionary measures while the investigation continues.Those conditions include reporting to the court every two months, informing authorities before leaving the city for more than 15 days, avoiding bars and similar establishments, and notifying the court of any change of address.The criminal investigation remains ongoing.Jadson retired from professional football in 2022, with his final club being Vitória.The attacking midfielder enjoyed successful spells with Shakhtar Donetsk, Corinthians and Athletico Paranaense, while also representing the Brazil national team.He was part of Brazil's squad that won the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup.At Corinthians, Jadson won the Brasileirão titles in 2015 and 2017, as well as the Campeonato Paulista in 2017, 2018 and 2019. He made 245 appearances for the club, scoring 50 goals and providing 64 assists.The case remains under investigation, and no final judicial determination has been made regarding the allegations against the former Brazil international.
Article Summary: Former Brazil international Jadson has been arrested in southern Brazil following allegations of domestic violence involving his wife. The 42-year-old, who enjoyed a successful career with clubs including Corinthians, Shakhtar Donetsk and Athletico Paranaense, has denied physically assaulting his partner. A court has granted him provisional release under a series of court-imposed conditions.

Article Title: Indian players counting on Women’s HIL experience at World Cup
Article Text:
(From left) Sunelita Toppo with Navneet Kaur and Kaitlin Nobbs during the Women's HIL early this year

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

When the Indian men’s hockey team ended a 41-year wait for an Olympic medal at Tokyo, the Hockey India League, which ran from 2013 to 2017, was cited as one of the factors behind the turnaround. Now, the women’s team too has something similar to draw experience from with the introduction of Women’s HIL last year.For the women, the biggest gain has been exposure — to foreign players, different styles of hockey and situations that are difficult to replicate during a national-team camp.“I think every player in our team has benefited from Women’s HIL. It has increased our confidence and helped us understand different match situations and movements,” said Lalremsiami, who will be playing in her third World Cup.For Neha, who played for Ranchi Royals in the last Women’s HIL, one of the biggest lessons came inside the opposition circle.“The players from other countries kept telling us that when we get into the D, we shouldn’t come out without trying something. We should keep looking for an opportunity and try to create something. I try to pass on those lessons to my teammates as well,” she said.That exchange of knowledge is perhaps even more significant for the younger members of the Indian squad.Sunelita Toppo, for instance, played alongside Navneet Kaur for SG Pipers, which won the 2026 Women’s HIL. It helped the two develop an understanding that they have now carried into the national team.“Sometimes, when I was running and trying to pass, the ball would go too fast or too slow, so the connection wasn’t always right. The strikers gave me feedback that if we could improve that connection, we could create better chances and score more goals,” said Sunelita.“I mostly link up with Navneet on the left, and they told me that if I could improve my body control and speed control, it would be a big benefit for the team. So, yes, I received that feedback and worked on it.”The benefit has gone beyond technical feedback. Playing together regularly has helped the pair develop an understanding that can sometimes make words unnecessary.“Sometimes you don’t even have to communicate verbally before making a pass because, through experience, you know where your teammate wants the ball and where she is likely to move,” added the youngster from Odisha.For another youngster, Sakshi Rana, the value of Women’s HIL lies in the experience of sharing the field and dressing room with senior players.“Our senior players keep sharing their experiences with us and motivating us. They tell us what they went through when they were our age and how they handled those situations,” said Sakshi.HIL, therefore, has become more than just another tournament on the calendar for the Indian women. It has created a bridge between domestic hockey and the demands of international competition. There is also a less visible benefit — financial security.For several players, particularly those from modest backgrounds, the league has provided an opportunity to earn significantly and support their families. That support can ease some of the pressures away from the field and allow them to focus more completely on hockey.
Article Summary: Women's Hockey India League has helped the Indian team gain exposure to foreign players, different styles of hockey and situations that are difficult to replicate during a national-team camp. The league has also provided an opportunity to earn significantly and support their families. The value of Women’s HIL lies in the experience of sharing the field and dressing room with senior players.

Article Title: From jumping a fence to World silver, 19-yr-old Basant Meghwal scripts history
Article Text:
Basant Meghwal (Image credit: X)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

JAIPUR: For someone whose journey into athletics began under accidental circumstances — jumping over a fence while bunking school in his remote border Rajasthan village — Basant Kumar Meghwal’s silver effort at the World Athletics U20 Championships in Eugene, Oregon then is an extradordinary leap of faith.In what is proving a breakout season for the youngster, the 19-year-old Meghwal scripted history on Saturday by becoming the first Indian athlete to win a world high jump medal.He had also clinched gold at the Asian Under-20 Athletics Championships earlier this year.In Eugene, the podium finishers all maxed out at a height of 2.21 meters, meaning final placements were decided entirely by countback rules based on missed attempts. Algeria’s Younes Ayachi clinched gold by clearing the bar cleanly on his first attempt. Basant secured a momentous, personal-best silver for India by clearing the height on his second run, while Great Britain’s Otis Poole took bronze on his third and final try.Meghwal’s run-up, though, begins differently. Not long ago, when he was in a field in his hamlet in Anupgarh tehsil of Sriganganagar district, lolling about the cattle instead of being in school, he spotted his physical training instructor, Iqbal Singh Maan, passing by.Fearing he would be caught skipping school, Basant leaped cleanly over a wire fence to hide.“His teacher saw that leap, immediately recognised his raw talent, and asked him to come to school instead. After that, he began to train him for the high jump,” father Gangaram Meghwal told TOI. “Before this happened, we didn’t even know what high jump was or that such a sport existed.”The path to international glory required considerable sacrifices from the family.“We still carry a debt of around 3.5 lakh rupees because sports expenses are extremely high,” Meghwal Sr said, “I am a dailywage driver without any land of my own, earning around Rs 12,000-13,000 a month to raise my two children. I took loans from relatives and private lenders to finance Basant’s training, proper diet, and equipment. Just a single pair of high jump shoes costs Rs 15,000.”
Article Summary: Basant Kumar Meghwal won silver at the World Athletics U20 Championships in Eugene, Oregon. The 19-year-old became the first Indian athlete to win a world high jump medal. He had also clinched gold at the Asian Under-20 Athletics Championships earlier this year.

CHENNAI: Australia have decided against playing a practice game ahead of next year’s highly anticipated Border-Gavaskar Trophy in India.Tony Dodemaide, who is managing Australia’s development squad that is currently training in Chennai, and is also part of the national selection group, explained that the tight international schedule leaves little room for a conventional warm-up fixture.Australia’s fourth Test against New Zealand is scheduled to finish on Jan 8, while the first Test of Border-Gavaskar Trophy is slated to begin on Jan 21.“So we’re playing Test cricket, as soon as the game finishes, we get on a flight and come here and have practice, and then straight into the first Test,” Dodemaide told TOI.However, he added that players who are not part of the playing XI for the final Test against New Zealand will arrive in India early to get accustomed to the conditions.“We need to win the Test match against New Zealand. But the players in the touring squad who aren’t playing in that Test will come early to get more acclimatised,” he said.The Aussie pace department may still be relying on the experience of Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Pat Cummins, but Dodemaide said the next generation of pacemen is not too far behind.“Scott Boland, Michael Nesser and Brendan Doggett have been really good for us, while we have some very exciting talent coming through. Jhye Richardson, Lance Morris and Xavier Bartlett have also played some one-day cricket for us.”Dodemaide also highlighted the importance of Australia’s current development camp in India, particularly for their young spinners.The squad has been brought to India specifically to experience conditions that are difficult to replicate back home.

Article Title: Will Kuldeep Yadav play? India coach reveals big selection headache ahead of Galle Test
Article Text:
India's Kuldeep Yadav (PTI Photo)

India spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule has allayed concerns over Kuldeep Yadav 's fitness after the left-arm wrist-spinner did not bowl in the second innings of the warm-up match against Sri Lanka Cricket XI.Kuldeep bowled 18 overs during the three-day fixture and had also delivered two-three overs before the match. According to Bahutule, the decision to keep him out of the second innings was purely precautionary, with the spinner keen to assess how his body was responding to the workload."Kuldeep bowled almost 20 overs in the sense 18 in the match and about two-three overs before the game also. He had a very good outing and he just wanted to take a break in terms of just understanding how his body is at," Bahutule said after the warm-up game.With Kuldeep rested, India gave their other spinners extended spells. Ravindra Jadeja and Manav Suthar bowled around 14-15 overs each, while Saransh Jain also had an opportunity to make an impression as the team assessed its options ahead of the first Test in Galle."Manav bowled about 14-15 overs, Jaddu bowled about 14-15 overs. So, they got a very good outing, they understood how the pitch reacts and I think it was a great prep for them," he said.The surface initially offered limited assistance to the slow bowlers but began to turn as the game progressed, giving India's spinners a useful understanding of the conditions they could encounter during the Test series."The bowlers had a great opportunity to go down and express themselves on a pitch which was slightly on a flatter side in the first day. But as the days went by, there was more turn on to it and definitely a good outing for the spinners," Bahutule said.For India, the warm-up was primarily about acclimatising to local conditions and giving players an opportunity to understand how the pitches behave."Preparation is a very integral part of coming on any tour. The reason of us coming at this particular juncture is to make sure that we adapt to the conditions, understand how the pitches are," he said."Most of the guys have come here, experienced guys, Jaddu has already played here. But the new guys like Manav and a few others, Saransh Jain, they need to just adapt to what will be the ideal lines, what will be the ideal lengths and obviously the field sets, which is very much important."Gill's recovery was another positive for India. The captain had been hit on his right hand during a net session on Thursday and was kept out of batting on the opening day as a precaution.He returned later in the game, scored useful runs and also participated in catching drills. Bahutule said there was no lingering concern over the injury."It was just a precaution more than anything else. And he has been absolutely fine. He has been doing his training. And the management decided that we could just take that precaution of not putting him into that first day," Bahutule said.The India captain has also been preparing specifically for the challenge posed by Sri Lanka's spin attack."Shubman takes his preparation very seriously. And he is a very meticulous boy. And he understands that whatever is the demand for that particular series with the attack, which has been successful for the Sri Lankan team. His preparation is done accordingly," he said.Bahutule added that Gill had been working on different scenarios in the nets, with India's coaching staff attempting to recreate situations he could face once the Test series begins.The warm-up also provided opportunities for India's lower-order batters to spend time in the middle. The team has been encouraging its bowlers, including Gurnoor Brar, to improve their batting contribution."All the lower-order bowlers, who basically bat in lower order, their contribution will always be very useful to achieve a good total in the Test match. And that is the entire process. We are encouraging them to bat as much as possible in the nets," Bahutule said.Devdutt Padikkal further strengthened his case for a place in the playing XI with a century in India's first innings. However, Bahutule indicated that the final decision would depend on the conditions in Galle."He expressed himself. He batted beautifully. And he is ready to, you know, whatever the decision, once we go to Galle, we will see the pitch."India are currently fifth in the World Test Championship standings, making the upcoming series an important one in their campaign."WTC cycle is a very important cycle. And every series is important. So, our effort is that, back of the mind, we definitely want to go there and win. And be a part of the finals and win the WTC also," he said.The selection of the spin combination in Galle could be one of India's key decisions. With Jadeja, Suthar, Jain and Kuldeep all offering different qualities, Bahutule said the competition was a positive for the team."All four spinners have that uniqueness. We have got experience with Jaddu. We have got great accuracy levels with Manav Suthar. And, obviously, Saransh has got experience. He has performed really well in domestic cricket. And that is how he has earned his spot," he said."And Kuldeep, being a wrist spinner, it always helps to have a wrist spinner in the side so that there is variety."With the warm-up completed, India will now turn their attention towards the opening Test in Galle, where the conditions and pitch will ultimately determine how the visitors balance their spin attack.
Article Summary: India spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule has allayed concerns over Kuldeep Yadav's fitness. The left-arm wrist-spinner did not bowl in the second innings of the warm-up match. Ravindra Jadeja and Manav Suthar bowled around 14-15 overs each, while Saransh Jain also had an opportunity to make an impression.

Article Title: 'That one thing completely changed': Ajinkya Rahane reveals how CSK transformed his IPL career
Article Text:
Ajinkya Rahane (PTI Photo)

Poll Vote & Share your view Should players reinvent their style as they age in competitive sports? Yes, adaptation is crucial No, stick to what you know 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

For much of his IPL career, Ajinkya Rahane was defined by one role: the anchor.Across 19 seasons, from the inaugural IPL in 2008 through to the 2026 edition, Rahane represented six different franchises and played 212 matches. He currently sits eighth on the tournament's all-time run-scoring list, with 5,367 runs at an average of 30.15 and a strike rate of 125.60.Yet despite such longevity, Rahane had to wait 16 years to get his hands on an IPL title.The turning point came in 2023, when Chennai Super Kings brought him into their squad for his base price of Rs 50 lakh. At 35, Rahane reinvented his approach and produced a version of his batting that had rarely been seen in the tournament.He scored 326 runs for the MS Dhoni-led side, but it was his strike rate that truly stood out. Rahane struck at 172.48 that season, a dramatic jump from his 103.90 strike rate the previous year. Before 2023, he had never managed a strike rate of 140 or more in an IPL season.Looking back at the first phase of his IPL career during The Indian Express' Idea Exchange, Rahane explained how his role had shaped his approach.“Before 2023, I think from 2019, when I left Rajasthan Royals then moved to Delhi Capitals and then KKR for a year, I think I hardly played.As a player, you always need that confidence. You need the surety to play with freedom. Before Delhi Capitals, I played for Rajasthan Royals for eight years and in between I played for RPSG. First three years I was with Mumbai Indians. So, it was always about the role that my team wanted me to play. I wanted to make that happen rather than going out of my role. So, the role that time was to be an anchor and then others will play around me. So, my strike at that time was around 120-130. And then I used to play till 15, 16, 17 overs, sometimes no till the end. But others were the attacking players around me.”The change began before Rahane even arrived at the IPL season. His preparation during the two months leading into the 2023 campaign helped him develop a more aggressive range of shots and, more importantly, gave him the confidence to attempt them in matches.“When the shift happened in 2023 with CSK, I had a good two months of preparation. And then I started working a couple of the shots. I thought ‘This is the time I should reinvent myself, probably play freely.’ The opportunity came with CSK.”That opportunity arrived unexpectedly at the Wankhede Stadium on April 8, 2023.Rahane had not initially been part of Chennai's playing XI. But an illness to Moeen Ali opened up a late opportunity, and Rahane responded with one of the most explosive innings of his IPL career.Walking in at his home ground, he smashed 61 off just 27 balls, hitting seven fours and three sixes. It was the first major glimpse of what became known as Rahane 2.0.“Actually, I was not playing in that game, but some injury happened. And then at the last minute I got an opportunity to play. When we had our camp, the CSK management had told me that whenever you will get an opportunity, we will back you completely. So, you just go out there and play freely.So, that one thing completely changed. I played with a fearless approach because I knew that even if I fail, they are going to back me. That opportunity came in Mumbai, where I scored 60 odd runs in 27-28 deliveries (61 off 27). That changed completely. But again, the preparation which I did for those two months, developing my game, playing different shots, that really helped me,” he reminisces.For Rahane, the transformation was not simply about suddenly becoming an aggressive batter. It was the result of preparation, a change in mindset and the confidence that came from knowing he had the backing of his team.After years of playing around the role assigned to him, Rahane finally found the freedom to redefine it himself. And it came at an age when many would have expected his IPL career to be winding down.
Article Summary: Ajinkya Rahane has played in 19 seasons of the IPL. He has represented six different franchises and played 212 matches. Rahane is eighth on the tournament's all-time run-scoring list with 5,367 runs at an average of 30.15 and a strike rate of 125.60.

The third and final day of India’s warm-up match against Sri Lanka Cricket XI at the Nondescripts Cricket Club Ground (NCC) in Colombo had a special spectator. Sri Lanka head coach Gary Kirsten was among those watching the proceedings, quietly strolling along the ropes before the small travelling media contingent recognised the familiar face.Immediately, smartphones came out, and the South African obliged before he bumped into Gurnoor Brar, who was taking a hydration break in the deep. A short chat followed before he walked up to left-arm spinner Manav Suthar, and then it was throwdown specialist Raghu's turn to speak to 'Guru Gary'. Both Brar and Suthar were net bowlers when the former India coach served as the batting coach and mentor for the Gujarat Titans in the Indian Premier League (IPL) from 2022 to 2024.Between chats, Kirsten kept an eye on the action as India's bowlers continued and occasionally looked at the giant scoreboard. The laps around the ground didn't last long before he went inside the NCC's main pavilion cafe.On the final day of the warm-up match, the turnout was better than on the first two days.The Indian team will travel to Galle having ticked most of their boxes before the series opener on August 15.It has been hard work for India since reaching Colombo on August 4. The visitors had two full-intensity practice sessions before every player got a decent hit during the three-day warm-up starting August 7. There was a concern about Shubman Gill's availability due to an impact injury on the ring finger of his right hand. After his absence from the first two days, the marathon net session and his 44-run knock on Day 3 helped India breathe easy on the final day, and later four sixes from Mohammed Siraj helped India win the match by six wickets.Gill's trademark drives returned, and the ease with which he operated wiped away doubts, if any, about his availability for the series opener. The Indian captain struck seven gorgeous boundaries, laced with exquisite shots, during his 54-ball stay in the middle.The management decided to give an opportunity to players who hadn't scored runs in the first innings, and the likes of Yashasvi Jaiswal, Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel got a decent amount of deliveries under their belt.Coming into bat after Jaiswal retired hurt for 61, Rishabh Pant looked very solid from the start. Unlike his usual belligerent self, the swashbuckling left-hander didn't worry after failing to score a run off the first 21 deliveries, and it was business as usual when he struck a six off the 22nd delivery he faced to get off the mark. The No. 5 is an important position for the team, and Pant holds a key role.Wicketkeeper-batter Dhruv Jurel gave him company in the final few overs. He is set to find a place as a specialist batter in the two fixtures. The right-handed batter got out cheaply again. But Jurel had scored a brilliant century and a half-century when leading India A against Sri Lanka A last month, which might be enough for him to get a place in the playing XI in the first Test.Before the batters checked the boxes, India's bowlers got a nice outing, with the Indian pacers Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna and Gurnoor Brar bowling at full throttle. Aquib Nabi, who didn't get to bowl in the first innings, too got an opportunity to roll his arm over. However, it was surprising to see no Kuldeep Yadav, even when the other tweakers, Ravindra Jadeja, Manav Suthar and Saransh Jain, got some overs under their belt.The last few days at the NCC in Colombo offered a comprehensive view of everything. A team captain was injured, old super fans came to greet the team they love, the support staff worked hard to ensure optimum preparation, and there was a surprise visit by the host nation's head coach.There were a handful of fans to see the biggest names in world cricket, but there was no chaos or pushing. Just a gentle raising of the hand was enough for the local supporters to establish their presence. Some got lucky with initials on their jerseys and miniature bats, but most were happy to sip some chilled beers while watching cricket.The setting will not be this casual when the action moves to Galle. India could well have Sai Sudharsan's replacement, and the game face will be well and truly on with crucial World Test Championship (WTC) points at stake. Guru Gary, too, would refer to the notes he would have made after watching the Indian players in action on Day 3.363 for 8 declared & 200 for 6 declared (Nishan Fernando 63, Nipun Dhananjaya 46; Gurnoor Brar 2/37, Ravindra Jadeja 2/33)357 for 6 declared & 214 for 4 (Yashasvi Jaiswal 61, Shubman Gill 44, Mohammed Siraj 32 not out; Keshara Nuwantha 2/57)

NEW DELHI: Just weeks before stepping into the ring at the Commonwealth Games, Jaismine Lamboria wasn’t thinking about medals. She was searching for answers. The recurring fever had refused to go away.Multiple medical tests showed nothing unusual and the Indian boxer tried to push through, managing the symptoms with paracetamol. When the illness persisted, she was admitted to a hospital in Mohali. Doctors finally diagnosed a bacterial infection, putting her on an intensive 14-day course of medication. For an athlete preparing for one of the biggest competitions of the year, it could easily have been the end of the campaign.Instead, it became the beginning of one of the most remarkable comebacks of her career. “I was avoiding further medical tests because the initial reports were coming back normal. We didn’t know what exactly had to be treated. Finally, after I was admitted, they detected a bacterial infection and I was on medication for 14 days,” the 57kg boxer said.When she was discharged, the clock was already ticking. Barely three weeks remained before the Games.“I started training only on July 1. Initially it was just warm-up, walking and stretching. I had very little time, so we had to be patient.”The physical recovery was only one part of the challenge. During those uncertain weeks, sports psychologist Priya Vrinda became a constant source of support, ensuring the illness didn’t break her confidence.“When I was sick, I was already connected with Priya Vrinda ma’am. She kept me mentally strong and never allowed me to go down,” Jaismine said. That resilience was evident when she returned to competition. Jaismine boxed with maturity, tactical discipline and composure to upgrade the Commonwealth bronze she had won four years ago into gold in the 57kg.One of Jaismine’s biggest assets inside the ring has been her reach in her category. While every opponent may not be shorter — Jaismine stands five feet seven inches in her socks — she believes her physical advantage has become an important weapon thanks to careful coaching. “My coaches taught me how to use my reach properly. It definitely gives me an advantage in many bouts.”
Article Summary: Jaismine Lamboria won gold in the women's 57kg boxing at the Commonwealth Games. The Indian boxer had been suffering from a recurring fever. Doctors diagnosed a bacterial infection and put her on a 14-day course of medication. Jaismine credits her coach Priya Vrinda with helping her recover.

Article Title: How Jadumani Singh's risky weight change nearly derailed his CWG dream before winning Glasgow silver
Article Text:
India's Jadumani Singh Mandengbam (PTI Photo)

A bold gamble after the 50kg category disappeared

The selection maze before Glasgow

Jadumani Si​ngh's Road to CWG Silver (AI-generated Infographic)

The Sports Ministry hurdle

Jadumani Singh Mandengbam (PTI Photo)

Why the gold slipped away

File Pic: L Sarita Devi (PTI Photo)

Olympic gold remains the ultimate dream

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: When Indian pugilist Jadumani Singh Mandengbam stepped onto the podium to receive the men's 55kg silver medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, it marked the culmination of a journey that had almost ended before it had even begun.The 22-year-old Manipuri boxer was one of India's standout performers, winning four consecutive unanimous 5-0 verdicts to storm into the bantamweight final before settling for silver against Australia's Jye Dixon. His medal also formed part of India's historic boxing campaign, which yielded seven golds and three silvers, making the country the No. 1 boxing nation at the Games for the first time.Yet, behind that success lay months of uncertainty, selection hurdles and a weight-category gamble that nearly cost him a place on the flight to Scotland.Speaking exclusively to TimesofIndia.com, former world champion and Jadumani's mentor, Laishram Sarita Devi, recounted how the young boxer refused to abandon his Olympic dream even when every obstacle seemed stacked against him.Jadumani had built his reputation in the 50kg category, winning medals at World Boxing Cups before learning that the division would no longer feature in the Commonwealth Games, Asian Games or Olympic programme.Rather than remain in a non-Olympic category, he decided to move up to 55kg — a division already occupied by some of India's biggest names."He continued to consult with me. Whenever he had to make a big decision, he called up and consulted with me — like increasing his weight category," Sarita told TimesofIndia.com."After he won a World Cup medal in 50kg, he got to know that the weight category is no longer in the CWG, Asian Games and Olympics. He wanted to move to 55kg."The decision immediately brought fresh challenges."Army had their No. 1 boxer in the 55kg category in Pune, who is Services' No. 1 boxer. And the weight category also has Amit Panghal — Olympian and Asian champion. He said he wanted to move up the weight to compete at CWG, Asian Games etc, but was discouraged by hearing questions like whether he would be able to compete at that level, which created a doubt in him," she said.Sarita, however, wanted only one answer: "We sat down and I asked him, 'Are you confident about the decision?' He said he was, so I told him to move up the category."The decision created another problem.Without competing in the National Championships, Jadumani could not enter the national coaching camp. But because he belonged to the Army Sports Institute, Services already had its designated 55kg representative. Attempts to let him represent Manipur also failed."We tried to make him compete for the state of Manipur, but we didn't get an NOC because he is with the Army," Sarita said.Relief finally arrived through a Boxing Federation of India (BFI) policy that granted direct entries to the National Championships for World Boxing Cup medallists. The move was aimed at rewarding elite international performers and ensuring they were not blocked by the usual domestic qualification pathways.The decision allowed Jadumani to compete directly in the 55kg draw despite the institutional overlap, resulting in multiple squad members — Pawan Bartwal, Jadumani Singh and Amit Panghal — finding themselves in the same weight-category draw.Sarita said her ward grabbed the opportunity with both hands."He then got a chance to compete in 55kg in the Nationals. Due to his effort, he won against the Services No.1, Olympians etc to be named Best Boxer in the Nationals. After that he got the chance to be part of the India camp," she said.He then cleared the final selection trials, which included physical assessments alongside ring performances."He participated in the final trial for the CWG and Asian Games — which had many aspects like strength and endurance tests before fighting in the ring. He won all of it to get selected for the CWG and was really happy and started training hard," she added.Just when Glasgow appeared certain, another setback emerged.Because Jadumani had only recently moved into 55kg, he did not possess the Asian ranking required under the Sports Ministry's eligibility criteria for Commonwealth Games selection."He got an explanation mail from the Sports Ministry, which put him in immense tension ahead of the Games," Sarita recalled.Under the ministry's guidelines, boxers were expected to be ranked among Asia's top eight in their respective categories."He was ranked No. 2 in 50kg, but he lacked a ranking in the new 55kg category. He had only competed in one Asian Championship in the new weight category before the trials for CWG and, being new to the category, lost in the quarterfinals," she said.That led to fresh doubts over his selection."He was disheartened when questions were raised whether he was a medal prospect because he was not in the rankings prescribed by the ministry. He called me and said the coaches were saying he may or may not be on the flight to the CWG because of this letter from the ministry," she recalled.The uncertainty only ended after BFI submitted a detailed explanation to the ministry, outlining Jadumani's circumstances following his weight-category switch."BFI replied to the ministry properly, explaining everything and after a lot of effort his ticket to Glasgow was approved. What I like about him is that he is the kind of person who doesn't give up and has a very strong will power," she said.Jadumani eventually reached the final after four demanding contests, each won by an identical 5-0 margin. But Sarita believes the scheduling ultimately worked against him."Jadumani's four bouts were very tough. He played all out in all the bouts till the semifinals as he got proper rest and recovery time. Since the gold medal opponent got a bye earlier, he had fewer bouts than Jadumani," she explained.The semifinal-final turnaround, she felt, proved decisive. There was a one-day gap after every bout until the semifinals, but there was no gap between the semifinal and final in Glasgow."Jadumani fought his semifinal in the evening and got the final bout the next morning only, so he did not get much time for recovery. If it was in the evening, he could have fought better. When he entered the ring for the final, I saw his face and body language sitting here and realised he had not had enough recovery," she said.The experience, she believes, underlines the growing importance of sports science."In such situations, we should look for how we can enhance or speed up the recovery process through sports science. We should discuss it to make sure our boxers can give 100 per cent every time they enter the ring," she added.Sarita first noticed Jadumani as a youngster competing in a local tournament."When I saw Jadumani for the first time, it was a tournament for young boys. His movement was really pleasing and I thought he could become a good boxer in the future. I identified him at that time only and gave him Rs 500 because I was very pleased with his performance," she recalled."Jadumani did not start with me from the grassroots. He learnt his basics from another academy. He came to my academy when he was preparing to enrol in the Army Sports Institute in Pune. At that time, I did not have any infrastructure and was coaching from a makeshift setup. And then Covid happened, we had to train in a very isolated small makeshift place,” she added.Years later, after training together through difficult Covid-19 conditions and watching him overcome one hurdle after another, Sarita believes Glasgow is only the beginning."We missed gold at the CWG, but we will work hard to get gold at the Asian Games for sure," she said.The bigger ambition, however, stretches far beyond continental success."His first and primary target remains Olympic gold. Commonwealth Games and Asian Games are the stepping stones in that journey. He will try to win India's first Olympic gold medal in boxing," Sarita concluded.
Article Summary: Jadumani Singh Mandengbam won silver at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The 22-year-old Manipuri boxer won four consecutive unanimous 5-0 verdicts to storm into the bantamweight final before settling for silver against Australia's Jye Dixon. His medal also formed part of India's historic boxing campaign, which yielded seven golds and three silvers, making the country the No. 1 boxing nation at the Games.

Article Title: Days after historic CWG gold, Dilip Gavit leaves without meeting Raj Thackeray after two-hour wait
Article Text:
India's Dilip Mahadu Gavit (PTI Photo)

Invited, but left waiting

A champion who made history in Glasgow

A journey built on resilience

Just days after scripting history for Indian para athletics at the Commonwealth Games, gold medallist Dilip Gavit found himself making headlines for a very different reason. The 23-year-old sprinter, who became India's first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medallist in the men's 100m T47 event, waited for nearly two hours to meet Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray in Nashik on Thursday before leaving without the meeting taking place.According to Gavit's coach quoted by PTI, Vaijanath Kale, the para-athlete had been invited to meet Thackeray during the MNS chief's visit to Nashik. However, despite arriving at the scheduled venue, Gavit and his coach were made to wait for nearly two hours. A video from the venue showed MNS workers requesting the duo to wait longer while trying to explain that Thackeray was occupied."We were waiting for quite some time... Sir is busy. We will meet him later," Kale is heard saying in the video before they eventually left.The incident came just days after Gavit delivered one of India's biggest moments at the Commonwealth Games. Clocking a Games-record 10.71 seconds, the Nashik sprinter won the men's 100m T47 gold medal, leading a historic Indian one-two finish alongside Mohammed Basil Morssinganakath, who claimed silver. The victory marked India's first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medal in para athletics 100m T47.Gavit's success carries a deeper significance given his remarkable journey. Born into an economically disadvantaged tribal family in Maharashtra, he lost his right arm in a childhood accident. His life changed when coach Vaijanath Kale took him under his wing at the age of 12, supporting his education and athletic development. After winning gold in Glasgow, Gavit emotionally dedicated the medal to Kale, crediting his coach for transforming his life.
Article Summary: Dilip Gavit was invited to meet Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray. The 23-year-old sprinter waited for nearly two hours for the meeting to take place. The incident came just days after he became India's first Commonwealth Games gold medallist in the men's 100m T47 event.

Article Title: How Harsh fought through pain to script CWG history, now targets Asiad medal
Article Text:
How judoka Harsh overcame pain

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Harsh Singh's right knee still swells. It still hurts. Every time the Indian judoka steps onto the mat, he is reminded of the ACL and meniscus tear that nearly derailed his career. But at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, pain took a back seat as the 23-year-old scripted history by becoming India's first-ever men's judo gold medallist."The pain never really goes away," Singh told TOI in an interview on Thursday. "Sometimes my knee still swells up and feels tight. During the CWG, I felt the pain and the knee occasionally got swollen. After surgery, the joint never became exactly the way it was before. There's always a little discomfort during fights. You have to ignore it and continue. The medal kept me going."The historic triumph came less than a year after Singh tore his ACL and meniscus while training at the Inspire Institute of Sport (IIS) in Aug 2025. Surgery followed in Oct last in Bengaluru before a year-long rehabilitation helped him return to competition."I was in rehabilitation for almost a year. The entire coaching team at the IIS, recovery specialists and Spencer sir (Mackay, S&C expert) helped me throughout.They rebuilt my strength step by step. Because of the IIS and their entire team, I was able to come back on the mat, qualify for the CWG and represent India," he said.The comeback demanded another battle off the mat. Months away from competition saw his weight rise to nearly 72kg, forcing him to shed more than 12kg to return to his 60kg category. Gold at a ranking tournament and bronze at the senior National championships sealed his place in India's CWG squad.Despite lingering discomfort, Singh dominated in Glasgow, with only a hard-fought semifinal stretching him before he clinched the historic title."The semifinal (against the Australian Pedro Carlos) was the toughest. In the 60kg category, even a small point can decide the match. We didn't want to concede anything and stayed aggressive," he recalled.With CWG gold secured, Singh has already shifted his attention to next year's Asian Games. Training stints in Japan and South Korea are part of his preparations as he looks to bridge the gap with Asia's best."I want to improve my speed, grip and strength. Japanese and Korean players are very fast, so training there will help," he said.Born into a modest family, with his father working as a daily-wage labourer, Singh once trained without owning a judo uniform. Support from the govt's schemes and a privately funded athletes' training centre changed the course of his career."My life has changed because of this medal. More people have started noticing judo," he said. "But the best compliment came from my family. They told me, 'You have made the entire family proud.' That meant more than anything else."Having conquered injury to create CWG history, Singh's next aim is clear — turning a gritty comeback into an Asian Games podium finish.
Article Summary: Harsh Singh became India's first-ever men's judo gold medallist. The 23-year-old tore his ACL and meniscus while training at the Inspire Institute of Sport. Surgery followed in Oct last in Bengaluru before a year-long rehabilitation helped him return to competition.

Article Title: 'I worked tirelessly while staying in Pakistan': Arshad Nadeem blames Glasgow cold for CWG poor show
Article Text:
Arshad Nadeem (AFP Photo)

Pakistan’s Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem has blamed the cold Glasgow weather for his disappointing performance at the Commonwealth Games. The defending champion finished ninth after failing to make the final three rounds, saying the low temperature made his body stiff and affected his usually smooth run-up.Nadeem managed 77.41 metres with his second throw after opening with a foul. His third attempt was 75.39m, leaving him outside the top eight.“The weather was extremely cold and I personally felt that it affected my body. As you have seen in many of my previous competitions, my run-up is usually very smooth, but this time it wasn’t… because my body had become stiff due to the cold conditions. My fitness was good and my health was fine, but ultimately whatever Allah wills is what happens,” he told reporters on Wednesday.Despite the result, Nadeem said he remains determined to make a strong comeback and urged fans to continue supporting him.“Please don’t lose heart and don’t stop supporting me either. Whatever I have achieved has only been possible because Allah blessed me with the opportunity to do it. The respect and recognition Pakistan has received around the world have come through years of hard work. I worked tirelessly while staying in Pakistan,” he added.“God willing, I will prepare with full dedication for the upcoming competitions and once again raise Pakistan’s flag on the international stage.”Nadeem also responded to criticism on social media, saying he understood the disappointment among Pakistani fans.“I have heard many things on social media, but I want everyone to remember that I am Pakistan’s son, and I always will be,” he maintained.Nadeem’s next challenge will be the Lausanne Diamond League in Switzerland on August 21. He will face a strong field that includes India’s Neeraj Chopra , Commonwealth champion Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, Keshorn Walcott, Anderson Peters and Thomas Rohler.Nadeem will hope to regain his form before the Asian Games later this year.

The defending champion finished ninth after failing to make the final three rounds. He said the low temperature made his body stiff and affected his usually smooth run-up.

Article Title: Glasgow to Ahmedabad: Gujarat receives Commonwealth Games flag as 2030 countdown begins

The Commonwealth Games flag was formally presented to Gujarat chief minister Bhupendra Patel on Wednesday, marking the beginning of preparations for the 2030 Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad.After returning from Glasgow, deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi handed over the flag to Patel during the state cabinet meeting in Gandhinagar.Sanghavi had attended the closing ceremony of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Sunday along with Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha.
