Article Title: Reality check after Commonwealth Games 2026: India’s boxing renaissance to face ultimate Asian exam
Article Text:
New Delhi, Aug 04 (ANI): Union Minister Kiren Rijiju in a group photograph with Indian boxing contingent (@KirenRijiju X/ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India’s record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism, but the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. After returning from Glasgow with a historic haul of seven gold and three silver medals, India’s boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.The CWG triumph underlined the country’s growing depth, particularly in women’s boxing. Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg), Jaismine Lamboria (57kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg) and Arundhati Choudhary (70kg) struck gold, while Sachin Siwach (60kg) and Ankush Panghal (80kg) topped the podium in the men’s competition. Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain, Jadumani Singh and Narender Berwal added silver medals.The challenge in Aichi-Nagoya, however, will be on an entirely different scale. Unlike the Commonwealth Games, the Asian Games will feature continental powerhouses such as Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, China, Chinese Taipei, Japan and North Korea — nations that have consistently dominated the World Championships and the Olympics.Uzbek stars Mirazizbek Mirzakhalilov and Bobo-Usmon Baturov, along with Kazakhstan’s Kairat Yeraliyev and Ablaikhan Zhussupov, are expected to headline a field packed with world-class talent.India will also be without two of its Commonwealth champions. Jaismine (57kg) and Arundhati (70kg) will miss out because their weight categories do not feature in the Asian Games programme, depriving the country of two genuine medal prospects.“The Asian Games for us is like the Olympics,” Boxing Federation of India president Ajay Singh said. “The best teams in the world today are Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and India, and all three are in Asia. Add a strong Chinese contingent and you understand why it is much tougher. You can’t replicate this (CWG) performance at the Asian Games. But if you win a sizeable number of medals at the Asian Games, you can be hopeful of winning medals at the Olympics too.Women’s head coach Santiago Nieva shared a similar assessment while insisting the team remains on the right path.“We can’t guarantee that we will win gold all the time, but we are on the right track. We know how strong the field will be at the Asian Games. The boxers are aware that they can’t sit on their success,” he said.India had returned with one silver and three bronze medals from the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. The Glasgow CWG showcased the strides the boxing contingent has made. But it’ll be Aichi-Nagoya that is going to reveal whether the progress is enough to challenge Asia’s finest and signal genuine medal potential for the 2028 Olympics.
Article Summary: India's record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism. But the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. India’s boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.

Article Title: Pakistan boxer Qudratullah ‘goes missing’ in Glasgow after Commonwealth Games campaign
Article Text:
Pakistan boxer Qudratullah

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pakistani boxer Qudratullah has reportedly gone missing in Glasgow, just hours before the country’s Commonwealth Games contingent was scheduled to leave for home.According to a report by Pakistani outlet Geo News, sources in the Pakistan Boxing Federation said Qudratullah was last seen in his hotel room at around 2am. Officials later checked his room and found that he was no longer there.The Pakistan team was due to gather in the hotel lobby at 9am before leaving for Pakistan. However, Qudratullah could not be found when officials checked his room, sources said.His passport and return ticket are reportedly still with the team manager. The incident is not the first such case involving a Pakistani boxer abroad, with another promising boxer, Zohaib, reportedly going missing during an international tour of Italy last year.Pakistan’s 21-member contingent finished the 2026 Commonwealth Games with only one medal. Boxer Fatima Zahra won bronze in the women’s 60kg category, giving Pakistan its only podium finish at the Games.The result was Pakistan’s lowest medal tally since the 1998 Commonwealth Games, when the country won one silver. Pakistan had also returned without a medal from the 1990 edition, making Glasgow its poorest CWG campaign in 36 years.Fatima made history by becoming the first Pakistani female boxer to win a Commonwealth Games medal and was later chosen to carry the national flag at the closing ceremony.Pakistan’s biggest medal hope, Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem, also failed to finish on the podium after serving as the country’s flagbearer at the opening ceremony.

Article Title: ‘Like preparing for IIT and UPSC together’: Father Murali shares Sreeshankar’s comeback story
Article Text:
Murali Sreeshankar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOCHI: S Murali gave an unusual analogy to describe the struggles his son, long jumper Sreeshankar Murali, undertook to regain full fitness after a career-threatening knee injury he sustained two years ago.“Sreeshankar’s comeback was as difficult as preparing for the IIT and Civil Services simultaneously,” he told TOI.Murali is currently near Prague, where he is closely monitoring his son’s training ahead of a busy stretch that begins with the World Athletics Continental Tour (silver level) meet in Bhubaneswar on Aug 22, followed by next month’s Asian Games in Japan.“Sreeshankar’s training now revolves around strength and conditioning, along with the prehab and rehab programme designed by coach Wayne Lombard. There is very little time to work on technique. The priority is to protect the knee on his take-off leg,” Murali said.His IIT-UPSC analogy aptly captures the magnitude of the challenge Sreeshankar faced after suffering the devastating injury just months before the 2024 Paris Olympics.Two years later, the journey came full circle when the 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last week’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.“Of all the medals Sreeshankar has won, this one gives me the greatest satisfaction because of the circumstances under which he achieved it. It reflects his mental toughness and hunger,” Murali said.The conditions in Glasgow were anything but favourable.“It was around 12 degrees Celsius with drizzle and strong winds, making the runway tricky,” Murali said. Despite the difficult conditions, Sreeshankar produced a best jump of 8.09m to finish second.The performance inevitably brought back painful memories of 2024, when the family received a grim diagnosis after Sreeshankar tore the patellar tendon in his take-off leg.“The doctors in Mumbai had not seen an injury like this. I thought he would never be able to walk again,” Murali recalled.“They told us it wasn’t a common sports injury but the kind usually seen after a serious car accident. His knee was completely ruptured.”Determined to find the best treatment, Murali travelled nearly 1,900 miles with his son to Doha’s Aspetar Hospital. “The surgeons reconstructed his knee using four screws.”The Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process.The painstaking recovery paid rich dividends. Since returning to elite competition, Sreeshankar has consistently cleared the eight-metre mark, including a season’s best of 8.38m at the Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar in June.“There is no time to bask in the Commonwealth Games glory,” Murali said, pointing to the demanding schedule ahead.Sreeshankar will now turn his attention to the Asian Games in Japan, where he hopes to upgrade the silver medal he won at the previous edition in Hangzhou.“With everything Sreeshankar has gone through, he has every reason to believe he can stand on top of the podium at the Asian Games,” Murali concluded.
Article Summary: Sreeshankar Murali suffered a career-threatening knee injury two years ago. The Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process. The 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last week's Commonwealth Games.

Article Title: 'You are still a role model': CWG medallist Tejaswin Shankar hails Vinesh Phogat, recalls 2018 memories

India finished the 2026 Commonwealth Games with 39 medals to its name - 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze. It placed India in fourth place behind Australia, England and Canada. Boxing and athletics produced the most medals (10) with weightlifting (8) and para-athletics (6) next in the order.In the truncated quadrennial event, held without shooting, wrestling, badminton, table tennis and field hockey, all of which have contributed significantly to India's coffers in the past, the country finished with 22 medals fewer than the 2022 edition in Birmingham (61 medals).Gulveer Singh emerged as the only multiple medallist for India at the Games. His silver in 10,000m and bronze in 5,000m made him the first Indian track and field athlete to win two individual medals at a single CWG edition.The Aligarh-born Naib Subedar made his international breakthrough with a bronze medal in the 5000m at the 2023 Asian Athletics Championships and followed it up with another third-place finish at the rescheduled 2022 Asian Games.The 28-year-old national record holder in 5000m, 10,000m, one mile and half-marathon trains regularly at the high-performance centre in Colorado Springs, USA, where steps towards his multiple feats and medals are forged.A Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) athlete, he's been assisted with Rs 30.40 lakh during this CWG cycle and Rs 25.32 lakh under the Annual Calendar for Training and Competition (ACTC).Behind every medal is days and weeks of training and preparation backed by government and funding by private players.Before the Glasgow Games got underway, the track and field athletes and para-athletes underwent training at the Spala Olympic Training Centre in Poland; boxers spent time in Belfast; the lifters travelled to Birmingham while the Artistic Gymnastics team set camp in South Essex.All such tours were sponsored by the government through its ACTC fund and TOPS.TOPS, a division formed in September 2014, operates as the Sports Ministry's flagship programme to support India's athletes win medals at the Olympics. It is presently headed by Col. Nachhatar Singh Johal, who represented the country in sailing at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.Earlier this year, TOPS' ambit increased to 27 sports with six getting priority: archery, badminton, boxing, hockey, shooting and wrestling.Subsequently, Target Asian Games Group (TAGG), which was created last year to provide support to select athletes was disbanded this year. It had begun with an initial pool of 16 disciplines and 37 athletes.However, its responsibilities will now be shared between TOPS and Training of Elite Athletes and Management Support (TEAMS) divisions. TOPS and TEAMS will manage day-to-day operations, development, and coordination for 27 specific disciplines.TOPS selects athletes based on their medal potential rather than a single qualifying criterion. The scheme assesses recent international performances, world rankings, consistency at the elite level, long-term progression and potential to win medals at the Olympics and other major events. Recommendations from the Mission Olympic Cell (MOC), National Sports Federations (NSFs), coaches, foreign experts and sports science teams also play a key role.Athletes are divided into two categories:Core Group: Established athletes with immediate medal prospects.Development Group: Emerging athletes being prepared for future Olympic cycles.Their performances are monitored regularly to ensure support matches their progress.There is no fixed annual funding cap under TOPS. Instead, assistance is tailored to each athlete's requirements, depending on their sport, training programme and competition calendar.Funding can cover:For athletes in high-performance Olympic and Paralympic disciplines requiring overseas training and advanced support systems, annual funding can run into several lakhs or even crores of rupees. Every proposal undergoes technical and financial scrutiny before approval by the MOC.TOPS follows a two-pronged approach—backing athletes capable of winning medals immediately while simultaneously investing in future prospects.This is achieved through:The objective is to maximise India's medal chances today while creating a pipeline of athletes for future Olympic, Asian Games, Commonwealth Games and Paralympic cycles.Athletes are monitored continuously, with periodic reviews conducted by the Mission Olympic Cell alongside NSFs, coaches and technical experts.Reviews consider:TOPS follows a performance-linked funding model. If an athlete consistently underperforms, remains inactive without valid reasons or repeatedly misses agreed benchmarks, financial support can be reduced or withdrawn after evaluation.However, genuine circumstances such as injuries, rehabilitation or long-term planning are also taken into account before any decision is made.Yes. TOPS has expanded beyond traditional funding to provide a comprehensive high-performance support system.Support can include:The aim is to give Indian athletes access to the same integrated support systems available in leading sporting nations, with greater emphasis on recovery, injury management, mental resilience and scientific preparation.TOPS says its funding decisions are guided by transparency, accountability and merit. Every proposal passes through multiple stages of evaluation involving NSFs, coaches, sports science experts, the MOC and financial scrutiny under government procedures.Funding decisions are based on measurable criteria, including:The scheme also incorporates periodic reviews, stakeholder consultations, documented approval processes and audit mechanisms to ensure public funds are used effectively. Its stated vision is that no Indian athlete with genuine medal potential should miss out on world-class preparation because of financial constraints.It is now 10 years to the 2036 Olympics, a Summer Games that India intends to host in Ahmedabad. If awarded, the goal there will not just be showcase its culture and ability to host an event of such scale but to compete with the best. To that end, the Union Cabinet has approved a revamped Khelo India Scheme and enhanced assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs).For the period of 2026-27 to 2030-31, which covers the 2030 CWG, LA 2028, Brisbane 2032 and five years leading to the 2036 Summer Games, a combined outlay of Rs 36,441 crore has been planned - Rs 29,054 crore towards Khelo India Scheme and Rs 7,387 crore to the NSFs.The revamped, and enhanced, Khelo India Scheme is nearly eight times the previous budget allocation (Rs 2532.22 crore from 2021-2026) towards grassroots development.After the positive returns at the Commonwealth Games, a tougher test awaits the Indian contingent later in the year at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan from September 19. And then further down the line at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, the necessary off-the-field steps for which have already been taken.
Article Summary: Neeraj Chopra won the silver medal in the men's javelin throw final at the Commonwealth Games 2026, in Glasgow, Scotland. Chopra will compete for India at the 2016 Olympics in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. He will be competing for India in the 4x100m and 4x400m relay events.

Article Title: 'A coterie hijacked him': Report claims Pakistan federation distanced itself from Arshad Nadeem before CWG flop
Article Text:
Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem (PTI Photo)

Federation 'distanced itself' from Olympic champion's preparations

Coach admits Nadeem was underprepared

Pakistan sporting structure under scrutiny

'A coterie hijacked him': Mentors question Nadeem's preparation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pakistan's Olympic champion Arshad Nadeem has found himself at the centre of growing criticism following his disappointing Commonwealth Games campaign in Glasgow, with questions now being raised not just about his form but also about the support system that surrounded him in the lead-up to the competition.The defending Commonwealth Games champion endured one of the worst outings of his career, finishing ninth after failing to produce a throw beyond 80 metres. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage clinched the gold medal, while India's Neeraj Chopra and Yashvir Singh completed a historic South Asian podium with silver and bronze respectively.But as scrutiny intensified over Nadeem's performance, reports from Pakistan suggested the Olympic champion had effectively been left to prepare on his own after the Pakistan Amateur Athletics Federation (PAAF) allegedly distanced itself from his training programme following a dispute over the retention of his long-time coach Salman Butt According to a PTI report, the PAAF largely withdrew support from the star javelin thrower after disagreements emerged last year over his coaching setup. The report claimed that several requests made by Nadeem regarding his training programme were not entertained, while the Pakistan Sports Board also did not release funds to facilitate foreign coaches or trainers.Instead of training overseas under renowned South African coach Terseus Liebenberg, who had guided him before his Olympic triumph, Nadeem spent his Commonwealth Games build-up in Lahore with Salman Butt and local trainers.The contrast with India's preparation was striking. While Neeraj Chopra completed his final rehabilitation and training block in Biel, Switzerland, fellow Indian javelin throwers Yashvir Singh and Rohit Yadav trained in Spala, Poland, alongside foreign coaches and support staff before heading to Glasgow.The differing approaches were reflected in the final standings as India secured two medals, while Nadeem failed to qualify among the top eight after the opening three rounds.Nadeem had arrived in Glasgow with limited competitive exposure, having competed in only one preparatory meet in Switzerland during 2026. He also trained almost exclusively in Lahore despite the vastly different weather conditions between Pakistan and Scotland.His long-time coach Salman Butt admitted the Olympic champion was far from his best and acknowledged he was underprepared for the Games.Former Pakistan Athletics Federation president Akram Sahi also blamed negligence and inadequate preparation for the dramatic decline."Since Nadeem's Olympic gold medal a coterie has hijacked him and never let him come to me," Sahi told Telecom Asia Sport."This result in Glasgow is hugely disappointing... the signs were imminent for the last several months as there was negligence and lack of training."Another mentor, speaking anonymously, argued that Nadeem had become complacent and failed to invest sufficiently in elite overseas training after receiving substantial financial rewards following his Olympic success.Nadeem's disappointing campaign has reignited debate over Pakistan's sporting ecosystem.Former Olympic boxing bronze medallist Hussain Shah described the situation as a reflection of systemic shortcomings."This is an athlete who is self-made and comes from a village and belongs to a low-income family. But he brought so much glory to Pakistan with his gold medals. And yet he couldn't prepare properly for the CWG. It is a sad reflection on our sports structure," Shah said.Pakistan's campaign in Glasgow also exposed wider concerns. Boxer Fatima Zehra, who secured the country's only medal with bronze, also lamented the lack of quality preparation and international exposure, saying better training could have helped her challenge for gold.The criticism did not stop with Pakistan's athletics authorities. Two of Nadeem's former mentors also questioned the Olympic champion's preparation, alleging that a lack of quality training and poor decisions contributed to his disappointing campaign.Akram Sahi, the former Pakistan Athletics Federation president who helped identify Nadeem's talent in 2018, claimed the warning signs had been visible for months."Since Nadeem's Olympic gold medal a coterie has hijacked him and never let him come to me," Sahi told Telecom Asia Sport."This result in Glasgow is hugely disappointing for someone who has risen to new heights, but the signs were imminent for the last several months as there was negligence and lack of training."Another mentor, speaking anonymously, echoed those concerns, suggesting Nadeem had not trained adequately after returning from Haj and had become overly dependent on official support."He won the Olympics after he got extensive training from his South African coach Terseus Liebenberg. His training stints at Northwest University Potchefstroom also helped him clinch Olympic gold. Now he waited for the federation and government to send him to South Africa for training.He should have invested in himself rather than waiting for someone else," the mentor said.The mentor also questioned Nadeem's current coaching setup, claiming his long-time coach Salman Butt lacked specialist expertise in javelin and that the Olympic champion had become distracted by business ventures after receiving substantial financial rewards following his Paris triumph.
Article Summary: Pakistan's Olympic champion Arshad Nadeem finished ninth in the javelin throw at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Reports suggest the Pakistan Amateur Athletics Federation (PAAF) 'distanced itself' from his training programme following a dispute over the retention of his long-time coach Salman Butt. Former Pakistan Athletics Federation president Akram Sahi blamed negligence and inadequate preparation for the dramatic decline. Former Olympic boxing bronze medallist Hussain Shah described the situation as a reflection of systemic shortcomings.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Relay flop raises Asian Games alarm
Article Text:
Vishal TK (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Even as India celebrated a strong athletics campaign at the Commonwealth Games — highlighted by three para athletics gold medals to go with five silver and five bronze from the able-bodied contingent — attention has now shifted to the disappointing performance of the mixed 4x400m relay team.The quartet, which made the cut after surviving a rigorous selection process that saw the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) reject all the other relay combinations, failed to deliver on the biggest stage.Vishal TK, who set a national record this season with a personal best of 44.98 seconds in May, clocked a below-par 46.1 in the opening lap in the final. Ansa Babu then struggled to match the quality of the field, clocking 54.1 while rivals, led by Jamaica’s Leah Anderson (50.8 seconds), comfortably ran under 52 seconds.Santosh Kumar Tamilarasan (46.4 seconds) and Rashdeep Kaur (53.72 seconds) were unable to change the complexion of the race as India finished sixth and last in the final rankings after Australia was disqualified and Zambia failed to finish.“It seems India’s top runners peaked too early this season. Rajesh ran 45.26 in March but his performance dipped in Glasgow. Rajesh is one of our key relay runners and, with Mohammed Anas and Amoj Jacob still recovering from injuries, he is now the most experienced member of the squad.It will take a miracle for our relay runners to improve enough before the Asian Games next month,” another coach said.Rajesh, who clocked 47.00 seconds in the heats, was replaced by Santosh for the final. Several coaches who monitored the team’s preparations also questioned whether the expertise of foreign coach Jason Alexander Dawson was being fully utilised.“Two coaches training two separate groups of athletes simply doesn’t work. Whoever can’t cope with Jason’s workload shifts to the Indian coach. Ideally, all the 400m runners should train under one programme and one brain,” one coach said, referring to the parallel coaching setup under Dawson and Raj Mohan in Thiruvananthapuram.A former national coach, who had previously handled the relay squad, urged patience. “You can’t call Vishal a sub-45 runner unless he consistently runs below 45 seconds. I’m optimistic our relay squads will bounce back and perform well at the Asian Games. Earlier, India was stronger in the women’s 4x400m relay, but now the men’s team has become more competitive,” he said.Meanwhile, AFI has reportedly decided not to field the men’s 4x100m relay team at the Asian Games while clearing the remaining relay squads.
Article Summary: The mixed 4x400m relay team failed to deliver on the biggest stage. Vishal TK, who set a national record this season with a personal best of 44.98 seconds in May, clocked a below-par 46.1 in the opening lap in the final. Ansa Babu then struggled to match the quality of the field, clocking 54.1.

Article Title: José Mourinho admits Real Madrid’s new signing 'lacks physical strength' after poor debut
Article Text:

Mourinho still wants another midfielder

Bernardo Silva's first appearance in a Real Madrid shirt offered supporters an early glimpse of one of the club's marquee summer arrivals, but José Mourinho believes there is still work to be done before the Portuguese midfielder reaches his usual standards. After handing Silva his debut in a pre-season victory over Ferencváros, the Real Madrid coach admitted his compatriot is behind physically following his summer break, while making it clear he has no doubts about the quality the 32-year-old will eventually bring to the team.Bernardo made his unofficial Real Madrid debut during the club's 2-1 pre-season victory over Ferencváros in Budapest after joining on a free transfer earlier this summer following the expiry of his Manchester City contract.The Portuguese midfielder came on at half-time in place of Brahim Díaz and played 48 minutes, initially operating in a deeper midfield role before Mourinho later moved him into the No. 10 position.Speaking toafter the match, Mourinho explained that Silva is still working his way back to full fitness after returning from his holidays."Bernardo has not had minutes and has only had a couple of days of training. It's very important, but the poor thing has had vacations," Mourinho said, according to Diario SPORT. "It is good for him not to do anything during the holidays and he has presented himself in a lower physical condition than he usually has and he has to grow, but he is a tremendous player."The Real Madrid manager added that moving Silva further forward during the second half was a deliberate tactical decision."He gives us the ball out, he can play as a 6, as an 8. During the match I understood that he lacked physical strength and I put him in 10.""It's another position that Bernardo can play well. For a coach it is perfect to have someone who plays well in three or four positions."Despite the public assessment of his fitness, Silva described joining Real Madrid as an opportunity he could not turn down.The Portugal international said he was proud to wear the club's shirt and is now concentrating on regaining full match sharpness ahead of the new season.His immediate priority is to build his physical rhythm before Real Madrid begin their La Liga campaign away to Espanyol later this month.Although Real Madrid have strengthened significantly this summer with the arrivals of Yan Diomande, Bernardo Silva, Marc Cucurella, Ibrahima Konaté, Denzel Dumfries and Carlos Espí, Mourinho admitted he still wants another versatile midfielder."We want a short squad, with 20 players plus the injured ones, which we have for some time, such as Rodrygo, Militao, Ferland (Mendy). We also need a player who can do what Bernardo does, which is play in different positions," he said.That desire has reportedly become even stronger after Rodri opted to join Barcelona instead of Real Madrid during the summer.For now, Real Madrid still have pre-season fixtures against Deportivo La Coruña and Schalke 04 before opening their league campaign. While Mourinho believes Bernardo Silva still has ground to make up physically, his comments also underlined why the club pursued the experienced midfielder in the first place: his versatility and tactical intelligence remain qualities the new Real Madrid coach values highly.
Article Summary: José Mourinho says Bernardo Silva is still working his way back to full fitness. Portuguese midfielder played 48 minutes in Real Madrid's 2-1 pre-season victory over Ferencváros in Budapest. Mourinho admits he still wants another versatile midfielder in his squad.

Speculation surrounding Thiago Messi's future gathered pace in recent days after reports suggested Lionel Messi 's eldest son could be set for a return to Barcelona's famed La Masia academy. The rumours spread quickly across social media despite the absence of any official confirmation, but the Argentina captain has now addressed them himself with a brief response that leaves little room for interpretationAhead of Inter Miami's Leagues Cup match against Atlético San Luis, journalist Bruno Vain stopped Messi to ask about the reports linking Thiago with a move back to Barcelona.The question was straightforward:Without hesitation, Messi replied:The one-word answer effectively shut down speculation that the 13-year-old was preparing to leave Inter Miami for La MasiaFor now, Thiago will remain part of Inter Miami's academy, where he has been developing since joining the club in 2023 following his father's move to Major League Soccer.Unlike Lionel Messi, whose career was built around his goalscoring ability, Thiago is regarded as more of a midfielder and playmaker.Speaking previously to Simplemente Fútbol , Messi described his son's style by saying:There is currently no indication that Thiago's development pathway will change, with the youngster expected to continue progressing through Inter Miami's youth system.The speculation was not entirely without context.Thiago previously spent time at Barça Escola between 2016 and 2019, when Messi was still playing for Barcelona, before later joining Paris Saint-Germain's youth setup following his father's move to France.His age also prompted fresh comparisons with Messi's own journey. At 13, Thiago is approaching the stage at which his father famously left Rosario to join Barcelona's academy and begin the career that would eventually make him one of the greatest footballers in history.The reports also surfaced only days after the fifth anniversary of Messi's departure from Barcelona. On August 5, 2021, the club icon delivered an emotional farewell after Barcelona were unable to renew his contract because of their financial situation, bringing an end to a remarkable era at the Camp Nou.While interest in Thiago's future is likely to continue because of his surname and family history, Messi's latest comments leave little doubt about the immediate plan.Rather than returning to Barcelona, Thiago will continue his football education in Florida as Inter Miami oversee the next stage of his development.For now, any suggestion of a move back to La Masia has been put to rest by the person best placed to answer it, with Messi's simple response ending the speculation almost as quickly as it had begun.
Article Summary: Thiago Messi has been linked with a return to Barcelona's academy. The 13-year- old is currently part of Inter Miami's youth system. Lionel Messi has responded to the rumours with a simple answer. Thiago will continue his football education in Florida for the time being.

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodríguez were nowhere near the church, but that did not stop hundreds of fans and journalists from descending on a cathedral in Madeira after widespread ruamours claimed the couple were set to marry there. The speculation grew despite public denials from Ronaldo's family, and ultimately left an entirely different bride and groom navigating an unexpected crowd on what was supposed to be their wedding day.Speculation over Ronaldo and Rodríguez's wedding gathered pace after reports claimed the couple would tie the knot on Saturday in, the Portuguese superstar's hometown on the island of Madeira.The rumours continued to circulate even after Ronaldo's sister, Elma Aveiro, publicly dismissed them. Responding to the reports on Instagram, she questioned why people believed Ronaldo was getting married whenwhile also criticising the continued media speculation surrounding the couple's personal life.Ronaldo himself also appeared to find the entire episode amusing. After a video showing hundreds of fans, tourists and journalists gathered outside Sé Cathedral in Madeira waiting for what they believed would be his wedding went viral on social media, the Al-Nassr captain reacted to an Instagram post shared by Jornal da Madeira with a string of laughing emojis, seemingly poking fun at the extraordinary scene unfolding in his hometown.ID@undefinedCaption not available.ID@undefinedCaption not available.According to ESPN, the rumours nevertheless prompted hundreds of supporters, tourists and media members to gather outside Sé Cathedral in Funchal, hoping to witness one of football's biggest stars getting married.Instead, the ceremony taking place belonged to another couple entirely.As crowds lined the streets holding phones and cameras, the bride eventually arrived—but it was not Georgina Rodríguez. A woman named Nicole entered the cathedral to marry Fábio, who was waiting inside for the ceremony.The confusion was later acknowledged by the cathedral itself.In a post shared on its official Facebook page , the cathedral wrote:In another post accompanying photographs of the crowds outside, the cathedral added:Although the unexpected attention created obvious disruption, some of the wedding guests chose to see the funny side of the episode.Speaking to local outlet Diario de Noticias da Madeira, one guest joked:The guest also questioned the rumours, adding:The wedding ultimately went ahead as planned, although in front of a far larger audience than Nicole and Fábio had ever anticipated.Ronaldo and Rodríguez have been together for several years and became engaged in August last year, when the Portugal captain proposed with a ring reportedly featuring a diamond estimated at around 30 carats and valued at as much as $5 million.Despite persistent speculation, neither Ronaldo nor Rodríguez has announced a wedding date.While supporters arrived in Madeira expecting to witness one of football's biggest celebrity weddings, the day ultimately belonged to Nicole and Fábio, whose ceremony unexpectedly became the centre of worldwide attention because of rumours involving two people who were never there.

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has played down concerns surrounding Mason Mount after the midfielder was forced to leave the field early during the club's 1-1 pre-season draw against Paris Saint-Germain on Sunday.Mount's latest setback came less than 20 minutes into the contest, with the England player appearing to pick up a knock before being replaced by Tyler Fletcher.The 27-year-old has endured a difficult spell since joining United from Chelsea in 2023, with a succession of fitness problems limiting his involvement and preventing him from establishing a consistent run in the side.However, Carrick suggested there was no immediate reason for alarm, explaining that the decision to withdraw Mount was primarily precautionary."He got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him. We've been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful," Carrick told MUTV after the match.Mount was subsequently seen walking without any obvious difficulty as he made his way towards the United team coach, providing further encouragement that the problem may not be serious.Mount has made only 25 Premier League starts out of a possible 114 since arriving at Old Trafford, underlining the extent to which injuries have disrupted his time at the club.Carrick was encouraged by United's overall showing against PSG, despite the French side taking the lead through Ibrahim Mbaye.Bryan Mbeumo eventually restored parity for United, who created opportunities to take all three points against the reigning European champions."I enjoyed it. Good challenge. Slightly different with the way they play. We should've scored more goals. It's good for the boys sometimes to have to problem solve and find their own way, and I thought we did that. That prepares them for the season as well," Carrick said.United have two more pre-season fixtures remaining before beginning their Premier League campaign against newly-promoted Hull City on August 22.
Article Summary: Mason Mount left the field early during Manchester United's 1-1 pre-season draw against Paris Saint-Germain on Sunday. The midfielder appeared to pick up a knock before being replaced by Tyler Fletcher. United head coach Michael Carrick has played down concerns over Mount's fitness.
